title: Settlement 2: Site Factors
subject: Geography
description: The main factors people looked for when choosing a site for a settlement hundreds of years ago.
author: L.M.

cards.front: Why do we think back hundreds of years when studying settlement sites?
cards.back: Many settlements were built before piped water, reliable transport, sewage treatment, electricity and internet

cards.front: Why was fresh water an important site factor?
cards.back:
For drinking, which is vital for survival

(Also for cooking and cleaning. It would come from a river.)

cards.front: Why was fertile soil an important site factor?
cards.back: It has good minerals, so crops can be grown for humans and animals to eat

cards.front: Why was grazing land an important site factor?
cards.back:
Land for animals to graze, to provide food for humans

(Cows on flat, clear land; sheep and goats on hillier land.)

cards.front: Which animals graze on flat, clear land, and which on hillier land?
cards.back: Cows on flat land; sheep and goats on hillier land

cards.front: Why was a fuel source an important site factor?
cards.back: Wood or coal to burn to create heat

cards.front: Why were building materials an important site factor?
cards.back:
Wood or stone to build homes

(Stone that was accessible and could be quarried.)

cards.front: Give two reasons high land was an important site factor.
cards.back:
Defence and shelter

(To spot invaders and have the high ground in battle. High land also provides shelter for the area below.)

cards.front: Why was flat land that doesn't flood an important site factor?
cards.back:
It is easier to build houses on and to travel across

(On foot or by horse.)
A coastline with a naturally sheltered area, perfect for a harbour

cards.front: What could boats in a natural harbour be used for?

questions.question: Which site factor would provide wood or coal to burn for heat?
questions.explanation: A fuel source is wood or coal to burn to create heat.

questions.question: Why was high land a good site for a settlement?
options: It is easier to build houses on
To spot invaders and for shelter
It has the best soil for crops
Boats could use it for trade
questions.explanation: High land was used for defence (spotting invaders, high ground in battle) and gives shelter to the area below.

questions.question: Which animals would graze on hillier land?
questions.explanation: Cows graze on flat, clear land; sheep and goats on hillier land.

questions.question: What made a natural harbour a good site?
options: A naturally sheltered coastline for boats
questions.explanation: A naturally sheltered coastline made a perfect harbour for fishing, trade and transport boats.

questions.question: Why was flat land that doesn't flood useful?
options: It gives shelter from the wind
It is easier to build on and travel across
questions.explanation: Flat land is easier to build houses on and to travel across on foot or by horse.
